themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Spike
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints surged to 10 THIS WEEK—a 700% spike compared to the 1.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.04)—suggesting a potential disease outbreak, pest infestation, or storm damage affecting Park Slope's tree canopy.
evidence: 10 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
700% increase with z-score of 9.04 (statistically severe anomaly)
Aligns with long-standing CB budget request for park tree infrastructure upgrades
reporting_angles: Interview Parks Department about whether a specific pathogen, pest, or storm event triggered the spike
Report on impact to neighborhood canopy cover and resident quality of life; compare to other Brooklyn districts

themes_detail.label: Curb Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 37 THIS WEEK—a 588% spike versus the 5.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 10.14)—indicating rapid street infrastructure decay across Park Slope.
evidence: 37 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
588% increase with z-score of 10.14 (extremely high statistical severity)
Converges with 598 street condition complaints in 90-day volume data
reporting_angles: Walk blocks with highest complaint density; photograph representative curb damage for visual storytelling
Ask DOT whether budget cuts or deferred maintenance explain the surge; request repair timeline

themes_detail.label: Commercial Activity Disruptions
themes_detail.summary: Three separate commercial-related complaint spikes emerged THIS WEEK: vendor enforcement (4 vs. 0.5 avg, +700%), commercial disposal (3 vs. 0.4 avg, +700%), and taxi complaints (3 vs. 0.4 avg, +700%)—suggesting either increased enforcement operations or new commercial activity strains in the district.
evidence: Vendor enforcement: 4 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 7.0)
Commercial disposal: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 3.77)
Taxi complaints: 3 complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average (700% spike, z-score: 3.77)
Active ULURP and waterfront development applications (444 Carroll St, 46 Nelson St) may attract new street vendors
reporting_angles: Is a coordinated enforcement sweep happening, or are street vendors/commercial activity genuinely increasing due to nearby development?
Interview local business owners and residents on whether trash and taxi congestion have worsened

themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Escalation
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints increased to 27 LAST WEEK—a 120% spike versus the 12.2 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 3.53)—paired with a broader 160% spike in general noise complaints (14 vs. 5.4 avg), pointing to heightened commercial activity or construction disruption.
evidence: Commercial noise: 27 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 12.2 weekly average (120% increase, z-score: 3.53)
General noise: 14 complaints LAST WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average (160% increase, z-score: 3.53)
1,151 total noise complaints (residential + commercial) in 90-day baseline suggest chronic issue accelerating
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify noise hotspots (e.g., Gowanus waterfront development, Carroll Gardens retail strips)
Interview affected residents and query 311 data for time-of-day patterns; check if construction permits align

themes_detail.label: Street Obstruction Surge
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints jumped to 16 LAST WEEK—a 313% spike versus the 3.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 6.17)—suggesting sidewalks or street passages are being blocked by construction debris, vendor setups, or abandoned items.
evidence: 16 obstruction complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.9 weekly average (313% increase, z-score: 6.17)
1,221 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (762 alterations) may be generating construction debris
Correlates with vendor enforcement spike, suggesting sidewalk encroachment as common issue
reporting_angles: Visit complaint addresses to photograph obstructions; determine if construction, vendor activity, or neglect is primary cause
Request DOB data on which active projects have generated obstruction complaints
